### Regular Expressions I

Write down the set of strings recognized by the following regular expressions.  
The alphabet is lower-case English letters (i.e., `a` to `z`).

- If the set is **finite**, write down **all elements** in the set.
- If the set is **infinite**, write down the **first 8 shortest elements**.  
  (If there are multiple shortest elements with the same length, any of them are acceptable, but you must prioritize shorter strings first.)

**Subproblem (3):**

b(a?b)+ | a*

### Ambiguity
#### Subproblem

Consider the following grammar:

\[
\begin{aligned}
S &\rightarrow S \ \text{or} \ T \mid T \\
T &\rightarrow F \ \text{and} \ T \mid F \\
F &\rightarrow \text{true} \mid \text{false}
\end{aligned}
\]

**Question:**  
Determine whether the grammar is **ambiguous**.

- If it **is ambiguous**, provide:
  - An example string with **two distinct parse trees**
  - An **unambiguous grammar** that parses the string uniquely
- If it **is unambiguous**, specify the **precedence** and **associativity** it enforces.
